title: Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE — Premium Revision Paper #4

pages.quiz:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #4
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which word ends with the sound /v/? (1 mark)
   A. half
   B. leave
   C. proof
   D. leaf

2. Which is the best first step to look up the word 'orphan'? (1 mark)
   A. Ask a friend to spell it
   B. Open at the letter z
   C. Read every page
   D. Open the dictionary at the letter o

3. Which word comes last in alphabetical order? (1 mark)
   A. uncle
   B. sister
   C. brother
   D. aunt

4. Which word has the long vowel /ɑː/? (1 mark)
   A. coin
   B. burn
   C. light
   D. market

5. What is the plural of 'knife'? (1 mark)
   A. knifees
   B. knifs
   C. knives
   D. knifes

6. What is the plural of 'leaf'? (1 mark)
   A. leaf
   B. leafs
   C. leafes
   D. leaves

7. What do we say when someone thanks us? (1 mark)
   A. I beg your pardon
   B. Excuse me
   C. You are welcome
   D. Congratulations

8. To skim a text means to (1 mark)
   A. copy it
   B. memorise it
   C. look for one word only
   D. read quickly to get the main idea

9. Which is a negative sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Money is for buying.
   B. I do not have enough money to buy a bicycle.
   C. I bought a bicycle.
   D. I have enough money.

10. Which question uses the pattern correctly? (1 mark)
   A. Do we have enough chairs to seat the guests?
   B. Enough chairs do we to seat the guests?
   C. Do we enough have chairs to seat the guests?
   D. Have we chairs enough to seat guests?

11. A red octagon sign with the word STOP tells drivers to (1 mark)
   A. go faster
   B. stop completely
   C. turn on lights
   D. park

12. Complete: 'That car belongs to my parents. It is ___.' (1 mark)
   A. they
   B. theirs
   C. them
   D. their

13. Complete: 'This bag is mine and that bag is ___.' (belonging to you) (1 mark)
   A. your
   B. you
   C. yourself
   D. yours

14. A balanced diet is a diet that (1 mark)
   A. has only sweets
   B. has only meat
   C. has the right amounts of all types of food
   D. has no water

15. Which foods help the body to grow? (1 mark)
   A. Sugar and salt
   B. Air
   C. Tea only
   D. Beans, eggs, fish and meat

16. You meet a new word while reading alone. What can you do? (1 mark)
   A. Throw the book away
   B. Ask nobody
   C. Use clues in the sentence and check a dictionary later
   D. Skip the whole page always

17. Which part of a narrative tells how it finished? (1 mark)
   A. The title
   B. The beginning
   C. The ending
   D. The middle

18. A dialogue is (1 mark)
   A. a poem with no words
   B. a list of nouns
   C. a picture only
   D. a conversation between two or more people

19. Why did Achieng tell Baraka to read his message before sending it? (1 mark)
   A. To print it
   B. To delete it
   C. To make it longer
   D. To check the spelling

20. Quantifiers: Which is correct? (1 mark)
   A. How much book are there?
   B. How many books are there?
   C. How much books are there?
   D. How many book are there?

21. 'Too much sugar is bad for your teeth.' Sugar is (1 mark)
   A. a plural noun
   B. countable
   C. a verb
   D. uncountable

22. In the story 'The Boy and the Borrowed Phone', what did Otieno do with the strange message? (1 mark)
   A. He replied at once
   B. He sent it to his class
   C. He typed his school name
   D. He showed it to his aunt

23. What does the proverb 'A friend in need is a friend indeed' mean? (1 mark)
   A. Friends should never ask for help
   B. A true friend helps you when you are in trouble
   C. A friend must be rich
   D. Friends are only for games

24. Which sentence shows two actions going on at the same time in the past? (1 mark)
   A. I cooked and my sister washes plates.
   B. I have cooked while she washed.
   C. I was cooking while my sister was washing plates.
   D. I am cooking and my sister was washing plates.

25. Which word needs a capital letter? (1 mark)
   A. week
   B. Friday
   C. morning
   D. season

26. What is the contraction of 'I am'? (1 mark)
   A. Ia'm
   B. I'm
   C. I'am
   D. Im'

27. In which tense is a narrative usually written? (1 mark)
   A. Command
   B. Future tense
   C. Past tense
   D. Present progressive

28. How do we speak about people who are ill? (1 mark)
   A. With fear
   B. With care and respect
   C. With jokes
   D. By ignoring them

29. What is the job of a comma? (1 mark)
   A. To end a sentence
   B. To show a short pause and to separate items
   C. To show a question
   D. To show strong feeling

30. How long should you rub your hands when washing them, according to the text? (1 mark)
   A. About ten minutes
   B. About two seconds
   C. About twenty seconds
   D. There is no time needed

31. Which conjunction shows a difference? 'The water looked clean, ____ it was not safe.' (1 mark)
   A. so
   B. but
   C. and
   D. or

32. What does proofreading mean? (1 mark)
   A. Writing a new composition
   B. Counting the pages
   C. Reading only the title
   D. Checking your work for mistakes

33. Which word has the consonant cluster /sk/? (1 mark)
   A. desk
   B. race
   C. goal
   D. ball

34. Which is the best answer to 'Where is the stadium?' (1 mark)
   A. At three o'clock.
   B. It is near the town.
   C. The captain.
   D. Hers.

35. Choose the word that means 'to listen with your ears'. (1 mark)
   A. here
   B. heer
   C. hair
   D. hear

36. What is a chorus in a song? (1 mark)
   A. The name of the singer
   B. The first word
   C. The last verse only
   D. The part repeated after each verse

37. Which sentence describes a feeling? (1 mark)
   A. We planted five trees.
   B. I felt proud of our work.
   C. We swept the paths.
   D. It was Saturday.

38. Which word has a silent w? (1 mark)
   A. window
   B. write
   C. water
   D. week

39. In the telephone game, why is careful listening important? (1 mark)
   A. There is nothing to hear
   B. The game is silent
   C. The message can change as it is passed on
   D. The first player wins by shouting

40. Which is the correct spelling of the colour of a ripe banana? (1 mark)
   A. yelow
   B. yellow
   C. yelllow
   D. yeloww

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Write the missing forms: good, better, ___ ; bad, ___ , worst; many, more, ___ . (3 marks)

42. Name the three groups of food on a healthy plate and give one example of each. (3 marks)

43. Write a short headline and two sentences for a news story about your school. (3 marks)

44. Give two safety rules for using the internet. (2 marks)

45. Write an invitation of three sentences to a wedding or birthday party, using 'invite' and 'decorate'. (3 marks)

46. State the difference between a factual question and an inferential question. (2 marks)

47. Write three sentences about your classroom using some, any and many. (3 marks)

48. List three things you can do to remember what you have read. (3 marks)

49. Write three sentences you would say to report an accident to an adult. (3 marks)

50. Put these events in order: (a) Omondi scored a goal. (b) Baraka spoke to Omondi. (c) The barber changed the blade. (3 marks)

51. Write two polite phrases you could use in a conversation, one to add something and one to give the other person a turn. (2 marks)

52. Explain what it means to speak with expression. (2 marks)

53. Write two minimal pairs for /l/ and /r/. (2 marks)

54. Explain the difference between intensive and extensive reading. (3 marks)

55. Put the adjectives in the right order: a (red, round, big) balloon. (2 marks)

56. Write three ways to make your speech clearer. (3 marks)

57. Explain how you can tell b from d when you write. (2 marks)

58. Explain the difference in position of 'enough' with a noun and with an adjective. Give an example of each. (4 marks)

59. Write four sentences using north, south, east and west to describe the position of places near your school. (4 marks)

60. Explain three uses of the comma with an example for each. (5 marks)

61. Explain why we do not say 'I am knowing the answer'. Give the correct sentence. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #4 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — leave
   Leave ends with /v/. Leaf, half and proof end with /f/.

2. D — Open the dictionary at the letter o
   Words are in alphabetical order, so start with the first letter.

3. A — uncle
   u comes after a, b and s.

4. D — market
   Market has /ɑː/ in its first syllable.

5. C — knives
   Change fe to ves.

6. D — leaves
   Change f to ves.

7. C — You are welcome
   You are welcome is the polite reply.

8. D — read quickly to get the main idea
   Skimming gives you the general idea.

9. B — I do not have enough money to buy a bicycle.
   It says that the money is not sufficient.

10. A — Do we have enough chairs to seat the guests?
   Enough comes before the noun chairs.

11. B — stop completely
   A stop sign means stop.

12. B — theirs
   Theirs shows that the car belongs to them.

13. D — yours
   Yours is the possessive pronoun for you.

14. C — has the right amounts of all types of food
   It has energy, body-building and protective foods and water.

15. D — Beans, eggs, fish and meat
   They contain protein.

16. C — Use clues in the sentence and check a dictionary later
   Context and a dictionary help.

17. C — The ending
   The ending gives the result.

18. D — a conversation between two or more people
   It shows what people say to each other.

19. D — To check the spelling
   Checking finds mistakes.

20. B — How many books are there?
   Books are countable and plural.

21. D — uncountable
   We cannot count sugar one by one.

22. D — He showed it to his aunt
   He remembered his teacher's advice and asked an adult.

23. B — A true friend helps you when you are in trouble
   A true friend is seen when we need help.

24. C — I was cooking while my sister was washing plates.
   'While' links two past progressive actions.

25. B — Friday
   Days of the week begin with capital letters.

26. B — I'm
   The apostrophe replaces the a in am.

27. C — Past tense
   Narratives tell what happened.

28. B — With care and respect
   People who are ill need care, not fear.

29. B — To show a short pause and to separate items
   Commas mark short pauses and separate list items.

30. C — About twenty seconds
   Rub for about twenty seconds, then rinse.

31. B — but
   'But' shows contrast.

32. D — Checking your work for mistakes
   Proofread for spelling, capitals and punctuation.

33. A — desk
   'Desk' ends in sk.

34. B — It is near the town.
   'Where' asks for a place.

35. D — hear
   'Hear' is what we do with our ears.

36. D — The part repeated after each verse
   The chorus is repeated.

37. B — I felt proud of our work.
   'Proud' is a feeling.

38. B — write
   In 'write' the w is silent.

39. C — The message can change as it is passed on
   The last player may hear a different message.

40. B — yellow
   Yellow has a double l.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: best; worse; most
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Energy foods such as ugali; body-building foods such as beans; protective foods such as spinach.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each group with an example.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Headline: Pupils Win Football Match. The school team won 2 to 1 on Friday. The pupils were happy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a headline and 1 for each sentence.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Do not share personal details; tell an adult if something worries you; use approved sites.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: I invite you to my sister's wedding on Saturday. We will decorate the hall with flowers. Please come at ten o'clock.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: A factual question has an answer stated in the text. An inferential question needs you to use clues and think.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each type.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: There are many desks in our classroom. We have some pictures on the wall. Is there any chalk?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Write new words and meanings; say one sentence about each chapter; draw a story map; retell the story to a partner.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct suggestion.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Help! There is an emergency. A boy has fallen and his arm is bleeding. Please bring the first aid kit.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each clear sentence.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: (c), (b), (a)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct position.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: 'May I add something?' and 'What do you think?'
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each suitable polite phrase.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: It means using the voice to show meaning and feeling by changing loudness, stress and pitch.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for using the voice and 1 for showing feeling or meaning.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: light, right and load, road.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Intensive reading is reading a short text closely, often with the class, to understand it fully. Extensive reading is choosing materials and reading a lot on your own for pleasure and learning.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for the difference in choice or amount.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: a big round red balloon
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for size first and 1 mark for shape before colour.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Open your mouth enough; speak slowly at first; listen to a good model and copy them; practise every day.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: b: stick first then the round part on the right. d: round part first then the stick on the right.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each letter.

58. (4 marks)
   Answer: With a noun, enough comes before it: enough food. With an adjective, enough comes after it: tall enough.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each position and 1 mark for each example.

59. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: The gate is south of the classroom. The field is east of the gate. The library is west of the field. The road is north of the school.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence.

60. (5 marks)
   Answer: In lists: rice, beans and cabbage. After yes or no: Yes, I can. When addressing a person: Mama, come here. Also before but/so between sentences.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each use and example (max 5 including quality of examples).

61. (3 marks)
   Answer: 'Know' is a state verb, not an action in progress, so it is not normally used in the progressive form. The correct sentence is 'I know the answer.'
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for state verb explanation, 1 for the correct sentence, 1 for clear expression.
